extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of aesthetics: artists, poets, critics, and philosophers
extracted.subtask_description: Theory-driven criteria for producing and evaluating works of art and poetry focused on achieving pure, objective perception (Platonic Ideas) and the psychological/physiological conditions that produce aesthetic genius and appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure objectivity of perception (disinterestedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge must turn away altogether from the will so that things are considered as if they could never concern the will at all; this will-less, purely objective perception is the necessary condition for genuine aesthetic appreciation and for the origin of genuine works of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the temporary elimination of volition (not an act of choice) and a predominance of intellect over will. Examples: perceiving an object without desire/aversion produces clearer, more objective apprehension. Anti-patterns: perceiving through motives, wishes, passions which distort perception and aesthetic judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as apprehension/expression of Ideas (Platonic Ideas/species)
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine work of art should reveal the Idea (the permanent, unchanging form or species) of things rather than mere relations or individual instances; art presents the adequate objectivity of the will at this grade of manifestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form and colour are media for expressing the Idea but are not the Idea itself (space and time belong to the medium). Art more easily enables apprehension of Ideas than reality because artworks lie outside practical relations to the will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production must spring from perception (not intentional abstract thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of every genuine work of art lies in purely objective perception (intuitive, pictorial knowledge), not in abstract, discursive, or intentionally willed concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should cultivate perception, since primary thought takes place in pictures; works produced from abstract intention rather than perception risk losing living originality. Anti-pattern: relying primarily on abstractions, rhetoric, or deliberate cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate the unessential; emphasize the essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should give prominence to what is essential and eliminate what is unessential, so that the peculiar character (species) appears distinctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concentrative framing helps present the Idea more clearly. Works that clutter with incidental relations to practical concerns reduce the object's objective clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic pleasure arises from cessation of will/suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: The withdrawal of the will from consciousness abolishes individual suffering and produces pleasure; aesthetic satisfaction depends on this will-less state enabling pure knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work that induces contemplative, will-less perception yields æsthetic delight. Anti-patterns: works that primarily stimulate desires, anxieties, or personal involvement undermine æsthetic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius: surplus perceptive capacity over service-to-will
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is the predominating capacity for perceptive (intuitive) knowledge — a relative excess of intellect over will — enabling original apprehension of Ideas and thus creating great art and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genius from talent: talent excels at discursive, goal-directed thinking; genius apprehends a different (more objective) world. Indications of genius include artworks that start immediately from perception and devote themselves to perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptive (intuitive/pictorial) knowledge over conceptual thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception (intuitive, pictorial knowledge) is primary and generative for deep thought and art; conceptions are abstracted, less determinate products of reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favour imagery and perceptual immediacy in composition; use concepts only insofar as they are derived from perception. Anti-pattern: elevating abstract concepts/genera as ends in artistic creation rather than treating them as abstractions from perceptual experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist/producer must be psychologically detached from the scene
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce (and to perceive) purely objective art, the maker must be separated, not personally involved or consciously pursuing personal ends; the necessary state cannot be an act of will but is a temporary predominance of intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production aided by being 'completely strange to the scene' and not actively involved. Anti-pattern: autobiographical preoccupation or conscious self‐promotion that keeps will active and distorts objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiological/temporary conditions fostering objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain bodily and situational conditions favour the temporary predominance of intellect over will — restful sleep, cold baths, calm circulation — whereas stimulants like alcohol/opium do not produce the required will-quieting state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To achieve the perceptive state conducive to æsthetic production or appreciation, cultivate natural means that quiet passions and heighten cerebral receptivity. Note: genius also involves a more permanent natural disposition (stronger brain/perception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of emotion and passion during perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Any emotion, passion, inclination, or aversion disturbs and falsifies knowledge; they colour and distort judgment and even original perception of things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works intended to produce pure æsthetic effect should minimize content that triggers personal desire/abhorrence in the perceiver. Examples: personal attachments, fears, or utility-relations render objects grotesque or repulsive in perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picturesque/poetical effect by presenting objects outside relation to will
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects or scenes are picturesque or poetical when perceived as indifferent to our will (e.g., in art, imagination, distant lands/times), because they enable purely objective apprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques to increase effect include novelty, strangeness, and transposing scenes to distant times/places to remove personal practical relations (e.g., setting a story in Italy or a remote land). Traveler's delight in a strange town exemplifies this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art facilitates apprehension more than reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Art (painting, sculpture, poetry) facilitates the absolute silence of the will and thus more readily evokes pure objective comprehension of Ideas than does real life, whose objects are often tied to practical relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create works that stand clearly outside practical concerns so that viewers can apprehend them disinterestedly. Anti-pattern: overly realistic works that constantly remind perceivers of practical relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species (natural kinds) vs. manufactured articles: focus on natural universals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Idea corresponds empirically to the species (natural kinds), whereas manufactured articles lack Ideas and belong to logical genera; art primarily reveals natural species (Ideas) rather than artificial kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming for transmission of the Idea, concentrate on elements rooted in natural forms/essences rather than purely artificial constructs. Example: Plato/Aristotle distinctions — things of nature have Ideas; artifacts do not.
